newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses face 1997 test after buoyant 1996.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses face 1997 test after buoyant 1996.

text.p: Several European bourses ended the year at or near record highs and many analysts predict further gains for 1997 as interest rates remain low and economic growth seems steady.
But they said trading next year would not be as smooth as it was in 1996 and some cautioned that it could be the toughest year since 1990.

It could mark the beginning of a bear market after strong gains this year. Analysts question how long Wall Street, the world's biggest stock market, can keep breaching new highs, setting the tone for other markets.
European markets, however, could do better than U.S. stocks in 1997, they said.
The London, Amsterdam and Frankfurt markets are promising a good start for the year. Nordic traders are poised for higher prices after a downturn in Swedish shares in the first months of the year.
East European shares should do quite well, too, they said.
Firm British blue chips took the FTSE 100 up 2.8 points to a record closing high of 4,118.5 in half-day trading on Tuesday, the final session of the year.
The FTSE 100, the key barometer of Europe's busiest share market, advanced 11.6 percent in the year as a whole.

The first quarter of 1997 is expected to be choppy for British shares on political jitters ahead of an election due by the end of May. The FTSE 100 is, however, expected to head into 1998 with further gains.
Trading on a freezing cold New Year's Eve was thin on the few open European stock exchanges as the closure of many markets slowed activity and a weaker Wall Street made traders wary.
Bourses in Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Brussels and the Nordic countries were closed.
The Paris bourse, which soldiered on until its normal 1600 GMT close on Tuesday, ended 2.9 points down, influenced by the weaker tone on Wall Street after a thin trading day.

But the CAC-40 index of French blue chips, which closed the year at 2,315.73 -- still short of its all-time high of 2,360.98 set in February 1994 -- has seen a 23.9 percent recovery over the course of the year.
In Frankfurt the main DAX-30 share index closed the year with a 28 percent gain on Monday and analysts said German shares should consolidate gains in 1997 due to growing corporate profits.

In Milan, Italian shares ended the last trading session of 1996 with slight losses, slipping from firmer levels in late business after keeping to a very narrow range in an extremely thin New Year's Eve session, traders said.
The all-share Mibtel index closed 0.2 percent down at 10,571 and the Mib30 blue chip index ended 0.52 percent off at 15,697.
But Fiat rose strongly following a government decision to give incentives to boost the depressed Italian car market.
